title: Handwired
brief: Cheng Lou's new toy project that compiles regular JavaScript — if-else, loops, state — into a neural net: no training, exact outputs matching the JS program, fully differentiable, runnable in a browser without a GPU. Demos include a mini OS transformed into a 9,909-weight network and unfreezing a compiled program's weights to train it in real time. - Warning: brand-new experimental repo (created 15 Oct 2026); the author frames it as "for fun", not production tooling.
details: Handwired is Cheng Lou's new project that turns regular JavaScript code — if-else, loops, and state — into a neural net: no training, exact outputs matching the JS program, and fully differentiable, all runnable in a browser without a GPU. The README explains the trick: program constructs are expressed as arithmetic (e.g. a comparison becomes ReLU terms), then the +/*/relu primitives are collected into a giant matrix multiplication that can also run on WebGPU. Demos include a small desktop OS transformed into a 9,909-weight, 130-layer network, a gallery where you unfreeze a compiled program's weights and train them in real time, and regex/JSON search over 100,000 documents compiled to WebGPU kernels for massive parallelism. MIT licensed. Useful as a mind-bending experiment at the intersection of programming languages and neural nets, and as a playground for differentiable-programming ideas; it is brand-new (created 15 Oct 2026) and framed by the author as "for fun", not production tooling.
